title: Jesus, Our Lord, Ascend Thy Throne
description: Jesus, Our Lord, Ascend Thy Throne in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 110, part 3, headed “Christ's kingdom and priesthood”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, our Lord, as-cend thy throne, And near the Fa-ther sit; In Zi-on shall thy power be known, And make thy foes sub-mit.

lines: Jesus, our Lord, ascend thy throne,
In Zion shall thy power be known,
What wonders shall thy gospel do!
The numerous drops of morning dew,
God hath pronounc'd a firm decree,
Jesus our priest for ever lives
Jesus our king for ever gives
God shall exalt his glorious head,
Shall strike the powers and princes dead

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
